mcq.question: `LOAN_DAYS` is defined in the class body of `Book`, not in `__init__`. What does that make it?

options.C: A constant that cannot be changed
options.D: A class attribute shared by all books unless an instance overrides it

mcq.explanation: Class attributes live on the class; instances find them through attribute lookup. Assigning `book.LOAN_DAYS = 7` creates an instance attribute that shadows it for that book only.

mcq.question: What is the purpose of `__repr__`?

options.A: A user-friendly display for end users
options.B: An unambiguous, developer-facing representation, ideally one that could recreate the object

mcq.explanation: `repr()` is what you see in the REPL, logs and debuggers. `__str__` is the friendly version; if missing, `str()` falls back to `__repr__`.

bonus.question: When should `__eq__` compare all fields, and when only an ID such as an ISBN? What changes if you also need the objects in a `set`?

Write a test that `Book.check_out` on an already checked-out book raises a clear error. Then write tests proving two `Book` objects with the same ISBN are equal and collapse into one entry in a `set`, and explain why `__hash__` must agree with `__eq__`.
